text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Sunday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Furore over meeting of Israel's Ariel Sharon and Palestinian leader Abu Mazen. Neither Foreign Minister David Levy nor Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai knew about the meeting.
- Israeli Arab member of Knesset who arranged meeting, Abdul Wahab Darawshe, calls meeting "a positive step".
- Two Hizbollah gunmen killed, soldier wounded.
- Foreign minister furious: The prime minister did not post him on the meeting of Sharon and Abu Mazen.
- Harsh criticism of Israel's Jewish settlement policy in report of United Nations secretary-general.
- Netanyahu promises Friends of Israel group in U.S.: Government to thwart bill barring distribution of missionary material.
- Legal precedent: Children can sue their parents for physical and emotional harm because of neglect.
- Levy and Mordechai to demand "explanations" for secret meeting of Sharon and Abu Mazen. Netanyahu intends to shake up his cabinet on Monday.
- Demonstrations in Hebron after Jews post "Mohammad the Pig" flyers.
- Bank of Israel could intervene in foreign currency trading to stop the accelerated devaluation.
